main_text.p: matrem potius dixit Theophrastus quàm patrem: latius enim patuit exhibendæ matris necessitas, quàm patris, quando & vulgò quæsitus mater ne- cessariò fuit alenda: in patre non idem obseruatum: vide Plutarchum & Laërtium in Solone.

ἀπάτης ἐκ κλοπῆς[?] Arcesi[?], inquit, solet furti adde, & aliorum criminum. sic apud comicum Agoracritus perfectissimum ἀποφίας[?] exemplum id sibi nomen ait inditum, ex eo quod perpetuo ali- cuius criminis reus in iudicio volutaretur. Notabis κυνολοχίαν[?] in voce ἀπάγεσθαι[?]: nam ἀπάγω, in furto Atheniensi proprie dicebatur de furto, sicut de aliis criminibus: auctor Vlpianus in Demosthe- nem Πρὸς Ἀπατουρίου[?]. quamquam alij veteres quibus potius assentior, ἐνδείξιν[?] & ἀπάγω ita distin- guunt, vt illa sit absentis delatio: hæc præsentis in ius abductio: quando aliquis manifesti criminis conuictus, in carcerem & ad vndecimuiros rapie- batur.
τὸ δεσμωτήριον πλεῖω χρῆν οἰκεῖν ἢ πλὴν αὐτῇ οἰκίᾳ[?].

Dictum venustatis Atticæ: sic apud Ciceronem habitare in carcere. Dinarchus Καὶ γὰρ ἀπὸ ἀττὲν ἄλλα ἕτερα δίκην ἐν τῷ δεσμωτηρίῳ[?] ἐν ἀνδρὸς ἡν ἐξεῖ[?] loquitur de Aristogitone, quem propterea actor earum orationum contra Demosthenis vulgò tribuuntur, ὁ ἔχειν[?] in carcere appellat, & alteri opponit recens carcerem ingresso, & vt ipse loquitur, ὁ τοτεῖ[?]. Demosthenes in ea Timocratem Aristogei- drotioni obiicit, quòd pater eius Ἀνστρατίδης ἐν τῷ δεσμωτηρίῳ ἀποθήσκειν[?]. Appio Claudio apud Liuium obiicitur pro magno crimine, quòd carce-

page.notes: Right edge of the scan is faded, so the last letters of several lines are doubtful. Greek passages are transcribed from a low-resolution scan. Many Greek words and accents are uncertain and marked [?]; treat the Greek as a rough reading only. The Latin "Arcesi" and "ἀποφίας" are doubtful. Line "ἀπάτης ἐκ κλοπῆς" is uncertain. The Greek of the Dinarchus and Demosthenes passage is only partly legible and should be checked against the printed original. Printed "sicut ... de aliis criminibus" has a damaged passage (the middle of the line is obscured) which may hide a word. The final word of the page is "carce-", hyphenated at the line end, with catchword "rem" at the foot.
